full_judgment:
24. In the case of Hajarilal Mondal and others vs Md Mozaffor Bepari and others reported in 8 BLC (AD) 77 it is held: It is settled principle of law that the lower appellate Court being a final Court of fact will have to discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the finding of the trial Court. In a case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate Court to reassess the evidence on record and to arrive at his own independent finding. In the instant case, the specific findings of the trial Court have not been reversed by the lower Appellate Court exercising its power under Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code. Accordingly, trial Court's judgment and decree are restored. 

 25. It appears that the issues in the suit have rightly been framed, considered and decided by the trial Court with reference to the evidence and material on record but the impugned judgment of the appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal as it failed to consider the evidence, oral and documentary, on record and, as such, the appellate Court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
